NO_IDEX_001 - for forest and mountain ecosystems

1. Aim

NO_IDEX_001 combines published ecRxiv indicator uncertainty distributions into composite indices. Version 1.0.0 contains indices for forest and mountain ecosystems, for year 2024, separately by region, for Norway, and for ECT classes. Values near 1 indicate better ecological condition relative to reference; values toward 0 indicate deterioration.

2. Datasets

First, we check which indicators are included in each index and where their results can be found on ecRxiv.

Indicator lists. Forest indicators are listed in data/indicators_2026.csv; mountain indicators follow ECA_2026 #104 in data/indicators_mountain.csv. Each row specifies the indicator name, ecRxiv ID, and ECT class assignment.

Source manifest. scan_git_indicator_sources() searches the local upstream git remote (main and submission-* branches) for published result files (CSV, RDS, parquet) and writes data/indicator_sources.csv. Optional manual or fork entries can be added in data/indicator_sources_extra.csv if results are not yet on upstream. This manifest is used internally when resolving result paths; it is not shown in the document. If the scan finds few entries, run git fetch upstream from the project root to refresh local branch refs.

Code 
# Refresh manifest from local git (upstream main + submission-* branches)
invisible(tryCatch(
  scan_git_indicator_sources(git_remote = "upstream"),
  error = function(e) invisible(NULL)
))

Registry. build_indicator_registry() joins the indicator lists with the manifest, probes each candidate URL or local path, and records whether results are available (match_status: matched or no_results). The tables below show the outcome for forest and mountain. Only matched indicators proceed to the analysis in Section 3.

Code 
n_sim <- 1000
n_years <- 2
report_years <- c(2014, 2019, 2024)
max_gap <- 5 # max gap in years to fill missing reporting years

registry_forest <- build_indicator_registry(
  here("data/indicators_2026.csv"),
  ecosystem = "forest",
  write_path = here("data/indicators_registry_forest.csv")
)

registry_mountain <- build_indicator_registry(
  here("data/indicators_mountain.csv"),
  ecosystem = "mountain",
  write_path = here("data/indicators_registry_mountain.csv")
)
Create forest table 
# Compact included / not-included overview (instead of long coverage lists)
registry_status_table <- function(registry, caption) {
  registry |>
    dplyr::transmute(
      ECT = .data$ect,
      Indicator = .data$indicatorName,
      ID = .data$indicatorID,
      Status = dplyr::case_when(
        .data$match_status == "matched" ~ "Included",
        .data$match_status == "no_results" ~ "No results yet",
        TRUE ~ "Missing ID"
      ),
      `Results file` = dplyr::if_else(
        .data$match_status == "matched" & !is.na(.data$results_path),
        basename(.data$results_path),
        ""
      )
    ) |>
    dplyr::arrange(.data$ECT, .data$Status, .data$Indicator) |>
    knitr::kable(caption = caption)
}

3. Analyses

Forest and mountain indices are calculated separately using the same workflow (calculate_index() in R/index_functions.R). The indicator registries built in Section 2 are the input to this section.

3.1 Loading and harmonising indicator draws

For each matched indicator in the registry, load_registry_draws() fetches the resolved results file and harmonises it to a common structure (year, part, value). Supported source formats include:

  • standard CSV (year, area or part/region, value or sampled_mean/sampled_value);
  • period-based CSV or RDS (period, area/region/region_code, value or sampled_mean/sampled_value);
  • regional RDS with companion national RDS (*_mc_regional.rds + *_mc_national.rds);
  • parquet (year, part, value or sim).

Region labels are mapped to NI regions (C, E, S, W, N, Norway) via data/region_lookup.csv. Each row in the loaded data is one Monte Carlo draw for a given indicator, reporting year, and region.

3.2 Reporting periods

Indicators do not all use the same time axis. Some publish single calendar years (year); others publish multi-year reporting periods such as 2010-2014 or 2020-2024 (period). These period labels also differ between indicators (length and start/end years are not standardised).

For aggregation we map each reporting period to a single calendar year using the period end year (period_to_year(), e.g. 2020-2024 → 2024). Where the source already provides year, that value is kept as is.

We use fixed national reporting years: report_years <- c(2014, 2019, 2024), and retain the last n_years of these (2019 and 2024 with the current settings).

Some indicators only publish one of the two retained report years — for example a first submission with only 2024 data and nothing for 2019. For indicators that are missing one of the retained report years, impute_missing_indicator_years() carries its nearest other retained year’s draws forward or backward to fill the gap, so the same indicator set contributes to every reported year. This is bounded by max_gap <- 5: if no other retained year is within max_gap of the missing one, the indicator stays excluded for that year rather than being filled with a stale value. With report_years <- c(2014, 2019, 2024) this simply means an indicator’s nearest retained year must be within one reporting cycle (5 years) to be carried forward or backward.

3.3 Resampling and aggregation

Aggregation uses ecTools::ec_upscale() with equal weights across indicators within an ECT class, and across ECT classes within the index (n_sim = 1000 by default). Steps 1–2 are run separately for each year and each of six areas: the five NI regions (C, E, S, W, N) and Norway.

Note that some indicators will have missing values for some regions. This will be describes in the workflow documentation for each indicator.

  1. Indicator → ECT — within an area, one draw is resampled per indicator within each ECT class, then combined with equal weights to give an ECT-level draw (aggregate_to_ect()).
  2. ECT → index — within the same area, one draw is resampled per ECT class, then combined with equal weights to give an overall index draw for that area (aggregate_to_index()).

The national index goes through the same two steps above, same as the regions. All indicators publish their own national (“Norway”) draws alongside the five regions, so each indicator’s value going into step 1 for the Norway area is simply its own published national draw, not a recomputation by us from the five regions. This matters because a published national value can reflect region weighting that is specific to that indicator - for example, the glacier area indicator (NO_GLAC_001) down-weights southern Norway in its own national value, because glaciers make up a much smaller share of that region (see ECA_2026 #76). As a fallback, indicators without a published national value get a synthetic one via equal-weight upscaling across the five regions (fill_missing_national_draws()).

This propagates uncertainty from individual indicators through ECT classes to the composite index without assuming independence beyond the structure encoded in the published indicator MC distributions.

No weighting is done between indicators or ECT classes: all indicators and ECT classes have equal weight (weight = 1). Individual indicators define their own regional weights to obtain their national estimate. Usually this weight is defined by the ecosystem extant for each region. There is one notable exception: NO_GLAC_001’s own published national value used the glacier area in the reference period as the regional weight, with the result of down-weighting southern Norway in the national estimate. We use these national draws as-is rather than overriding it with an equal-weight regional average.

3.3.1 Direct national aggregation (no ECT step)

We also calculate a direct national index that skips the ECT step: every matched indicator is resampled directly to the index with equal weight (aggregate_indicators_to_index_direct()), rather than first being equal-weighted within its ECT class. This means an ECT class with many indicators has proportionally more influence on this version of the index than it does in the ECT-based workflow, where each ECT class counts equally regardless of how many indicators it contains.

This direct aggregation is computed independently, and reported alongside the ECT-based index (tagged "Index (direct)" in the results) so the two can be compared. Note that the indicator ID NO_IDEX_001 retains to the hierarchically aggregated version.

3.4 Summaries

The full MC distributions (all areas) are stored for export. For reporting we summarise each ECT class and the overall index by the median and an approximate 95% interval (2.5% and 97.5% quantiles). Regional and national (Norway) indices are both calculated by the same steps 1–2 above, since Norway is treated as just another area (see Section 3).

Calculate forest index 
forest_index <- calculate_index(
  registry_forest |> filter(match_status == "matched"),
  n_sim = n_sim,
  n_years = n_years,
  report_years = report_years,
  max_gap = max_gap,
  include_direct_index = TRUE
)

saveRDS(forest_index, here::here("data/forest_index_170826.rds"))
Code 
forest_index <- readRDS(here::here("data/forest_index_170826.rds"))

Code 
forest_index$coverage |>
  select(year, part, "# indicators" = n_indicators, "# indicators imputed" = n_indicators_imputed, "# indicators observed" = n_indicators_observed) |>
  gt::gt()
Code 
# Single-indicator test: with one matched indicator, the index for any area
# (including Norway, using that indicator's own published national draws)
# equals that indicator's own draws for the same area.
if (sum(registry_mountain$match_status == "matched") >= 1) {
  one_reg <- registry_mountain |> filter(match_status == "matched") |> slice(1)
  one_out <- calculate_index(one_reg, n_sim = 200, n_years = 1, report_years = report_years, max_gap = max_gap)
  part_chk <- one_out$indicator_draws |>
    distinct(part) |>
    arrange(part) |>
    slice(1) |>
    pull(part)
  val_one <- one_out$summaries |>
    filter(level == "Index", part == part_chk) |>
    slice(1)
  src <- one_out$indicator_draws |>
    filter(part == part_chk) |>
    summarise(median = median(value), .groups = "drop")
  stopifnot(abs(val_one$median - src$median) < 0.05)
}

5. Export file

The exported files contain the full MC distributions for every level ("ECT", "Index", and the alternative "Index (direct)", see Section 3), area, and year — identifiable via the level and id columns.

Code 
export_index_results(
  forest_index$distributions,
  here("data/results_NO_IDEX_001_forest_v1.0.0.csv")
)

export_index_results(
  mountain_index$distributions,
  here("data/results_NO_IDEX_001_mountain_v1.0.0.csv")
)
